## Data Cleaning

### Cleaning data to prepare for ANOVA

```{r}
# view raw Height data set
Height_Data_Raw

# checking the counts of rows and columns to checj if the dataset size is correct
nrow(Height_Data_Raw)
dim(Height_Data_Raw)
glimpse(Height_Data_Raw)

# checking column numbers and names
# checking to make sure they are tidy
ncol(Height_Data_Raw)
names(Height_Data_Raw)

# checking unique values in treatment column
# looking for any formatting issues or typos
unique(Height_Data_Raw$Treatment)
## NAs will need to be filtered out

# irregular values
summary(Height_Data_Raw$Seedling_Ht_cm)

which(Height_Data_Raw$Seedling_Ht_cm == 0.0)

# histogram with proper labels
ggplot(Height_Data_Raw) +
  aes(x = Seedling_Ht_cm) +
  geom_histogram() +
  labs(
    x = "Seedling Height (cm)",
    y = "Number of Seedlings"
  )

## should display a large number of dead seedlings at 0 cm

# start cleaning
Height_Data_Clean <- Height_Data_Raw |> 
  # filter out dead seedlings to remove 0.0 values
  filter(Dead_Alive == "Alive") |> 
  # filter out rows where Seedling_Ht_cm is NA
  filter(!is.na(Seedling_Ht_cm)) |> 
  # convert treatment into a factor
  mutate(Treatment = as.factor(Treatment))
# clean data
Height_Data_Clean
```

```{r}
# view raw Soil Moisture data set
Moist_Data_Raw

# checking the counts of rows and columns to checj if the dataset size is correct
nrow(Moist_Data_Raw)
dim(Moist_Data_Raw)
glimpse(Moist_Data_Raw)

# checking column numbers and names
# checking to make sure they are tidy
ncol(Moist_Data_Raw)
names(Moist_Data_Raw)

# checking unique values in treatment column
# looking for any formatting issues or typos
unique(Moist_Data_Raw$FLAG)
## NAs will need to be filtered out

# start cleaning
Moist_Data_Clean <- Moist_Data_Raw |> 
# convert to double
  mutate(
    VWC1_perc = as.double(VWC1_perc),
    VWC2_perc = as.double(VWC2_perc),
    VWC3_perc = as.double(VWC3_perc)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    VWC_Mean = mean(c(VWC1_perc, VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc), na.rm = TRUE)
  )
# clean data
Moist_Data_Clean
```

### Cleaning data to prepare for Regression

```{r}
# view raw SPAD data set
SPAD_Data_Raw
# start cleaning
SPAD_Data_Clean <- SPAD_Data_Raw |> 
  # filter out dead saplings, keeping observations that are alive
  filter(Dead_Alive == "Alive") |> 
  # filter out rows wher Tag Number is blank
  filter(Tag_Num != "") |> 
  # calculate average leaf value among all 6 columns
  mutate(Leaf_Average = (Leaf1 + Leaf2 + Leaf3 + Leaf4 + Leaf5 + Leaf6)/6) |> 
  mutate(
    Treatment = as.factor(Treatment),
    Date = as.factor(Date)
  )
SPAD_Data_Clean
```

## ANOVA

### Does soil moisture treatment significantly influence leaf chlorophyll content (SPAD)? Does leaf chlorophyll content change between October 8th, 2026, and October 15th, 2026? Is there an interaction effect between the soil moisture treatment and the date on SPAD?

Null Hypothesis (H0): There is no significant difference in mean leaf chlorophyll content (SPAD) across different soil moisture treatments, dates, or their interaction.

Alternative Hypothesis (HA): There is a significant difference in mean leaf chlorophyll content (SPAD) based on soil moisture treatment, date, or their interaction. Specifically, the impact of the moisture treatment on SPAD depends on which date is being observed.

```{r}
# assumption/normality test
model_SPAD <- lm(Leaf_Average ~ Treatment * Date, data = SPAD_Data_Clean)

plot(model_SPAD, which = 1)
plot(model_SPAD, which = 2)

# creating a QQ plot of residuals
ggpubr::ggqqplot(residuals(model_SPAD))

# levene's test
SPAD_Data_Clean |> 
  rstatix::levene_test(Leaf_Average ~ Treatment * Date)
```

```{r}
# statistical test

# method 2 from lab 6 (two-way anova): using aov() and summary() to prepare for the Tukey HSD check
model_SPAD_aov <- aov(Leaf_Average ~ Treatment * Date, data = SPAD_Data_Clean)
# summary
summary(model_SPAD_aov)

# pairwise differences post-hoc check
TukeyHSD(model_SPAD_aov)
```

```{r}
# nice figure

# calculate the summary statistics
SPAD_summary <- SPAD_Data_Clean |> 
  group_by(Date, Treatment) |> 
  summarise(
    mean = mean(Leaf_Average), 
    se = sd(Leaf_Average) / sqrt(length(Leaf_Average)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# bar chart
ggplot(SPAD_summary) + 
  aes(x = Date, y = mean, fill = Treatment) + 
  geom_col(position = "dodge") + 
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se), position = position_dodge(0.9), width = 0.2) +
  labs(
    x = "Sampling Date",
    y = "Mean Leaf Chlorophyll Content (SPAD)",
    fill = "Treatment"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

## Regression

### Does sapling height significantly predict the total leaf count of an individual sapling?

Null hypothesis (H0): Sapling height does not significantly predict leaf count. Taller saplings do not systematically have more or fewer leaves than shorter saplings (the true population slope is equal to zero).

Alternative Hypothesis (HA): Sapling height significantly predicts leaf count. As sapling height increases, the total leaf count changes in a predictable linear trend.

```{r}
# before beginning...

# ensure both use factor
Height_Data_Clean <- Height_Data_Clean |> 
  mutate(Date = as.factor(Date))

# join the two data sets
Reg_Data <- inner_join(Height_Data_Clean, SPAD_Data_Clean, by = c("Tag_Num", "Date"))

# checking if the names are as i need them
names(Reg_Data)
```

```{r}
# assumption/normality test

# ensure Num_leaves is numeric and has no missing values
Reg_Data <- Reg_Data |> 
  mutate(Num_leaves = as.numeric(Num_leaves)) |> 
  filter(!is.na(Num_leaves))

# visualize the data to check for linear relationship
ggplot(Reg_Data) + 
  aes(Seedling_Ht_cm, Num_leaves) +
  geom_point()

# check normality of the response variable using a histogram
hist(Reg_Data$Num_leaves)
hist(Reg_Data$Seedling_Ht_cm)

# check homoscedasticity (equal variance)
height.lm <- lm(Num_leaves ~ Seedling_Ht_cm, data = Reg_Data)
plot(height.lm, which = 1)
```

```{r}
# statistical test

# fit the simple linear regression model
height.lm <- lm(Num_leaves ~ Seedling_Ht_cm, data = Reg_Data)
height.lm
summary(height.lm)

# extract slope and intercept
slope <- coef(height.lm)[2]
slope

int <- coef(height.lm)[1]
int

# extract p-value for slope
summary(height.lm)$coefficients[2, 4]

# extract R-squared value
Rsq <- summary(height.lm)$r.squared
Rsq
```

```{r}
# nice figure

# plot dat regression
Height_plot <- ggplot(Reg_Data) + 
  aes(Seedling_Ht_cm, Num_leaves) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    x = "Seedling Height (cm)",
    y = "Total Leaf Count"
  )

Height_plot
```
